description:
## Context

`src/fetcher/crest_http_client.cr` is **531 lines** — the largest source file in the
codebase. A single class currently carries **at least five unrelated responsibilities**:

| Lines (approx) | Concern |
|---|---|
| ~80–100, 160–190, 380–395 | HTTP request orchestration (semaphore, perform_request, redirect chain, response conversion) |
| ~200–290, plus helper chain | **Redirect policy & validation** (allow_redirect?, same_domain_redirect?, subdomain_redirect?, external_redirect_allowed?, permanent_redirect?, allowed_domain_redirect?, same_registrable_domain?, validate_redirect_target, validate_redirect_domain, resolve_redirect_url) |
| ~30–50, 355–420, 460–490 | **DNS cache management** (class-level @@dns_cache, @@dns_cache_lock, ensure_dns_cleanup_registered, dns_max_entries, get_cached_dns, cache_dns, enforce_dns_limit, clear_dns_cache, clear_expired_dns) |
| ~425–465 | **DNS rebinding checks** (verify_dns_rebinding, resolve_and_validate_new_dns, validate_address_for_host, …) |
| ~495–545 | **Error mapping** (handle_error + 6 private handle_*_error methods) |
| ~545–560 | TLS/SSL bypass acknowledgement |

This violates SRP and makes the class hard to test, hard to reason about, and the
mix of class-level `@@` state (DNS cache) with per-instance state muddles the
ownership model.

## Goal

Split into focused units, each in its own file. Each unit is independently testable
and has a single, clear job. Public API of `CrestHttpClient` stays unchanged so
callers (`Fetcher::Reddit`, `Fetcher::Software`, etc.) and the existing spec files
keep working.

## Non-goals

- No behavior changes. Tests must pass with no spec edits beyond the uncommitted
  `spec/dns_cache_spec.cr` require line being folded in.
- No new public API surface.

## Children

See the wired-up child tickets. They are sequenced:

1. Fold the uncommitted `spec/dns_cache_spec.cr` require into the first commit.
2. Extract `DNSCache` (class-level state → instance class).
3. Extract `RedirectPolicy` (the policy methods are pure functions of inputs).
4. Extract `ErrorMapper` (the case/handler methods).
5. Extract `RebindingChecker` (depends on DNSCache).
6. DRY: collapse duplicated `Crest::Request.execute` call between
   `perform_request` and `perform_follow_redirect`.
7. Cleanup: remove redundant `extract_domain` wrapper, rename `transition_domain`.
8. Run full spec suite.

## Definition of done

- `just spec` (or equivalent) passes.
- `crest_http_client.cr` is materially shorter and contains only orchestration
  + delegation.
- Each extracted unit lives in `src/fetcher/crest_http_client/<name>.cr`.

comments.text: Merged with fetcherc-tbk (closed as duplicate). Preserving additional reliability findings from tbk as new children: fetcherc-c1h.9 (dead branch in resolve_redirect_url), fetcherc-c1h.10 (DNS cache cleanup registration leak — class-level singleton outlives per-instance config), fetcherc-c1h.11 (transition_domain records success on target before contact), fetcherc-c1h.12 (DNSError over-use — collapses non-DNS errors and loses type info).

title: Refactor CrestHttpClient for SRP and reliability
